executiveSummary: GM1706 passes the complete deterministic model contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. The 2025 CBS identity, generalized boundary, 21,665 residents, twenty neighbourhoods, six BAG places, twenty-one BRT settlements, Maarheeze station, 42 transit stop areas and two section-verified A2 logical corridors are coherent. Official nulls, exact zero-intensity behavior, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, event-attributable essential-service person-hours and map-layer invariance also pass. Release remains correction-required for two municipality-specific manifestations of shared model defects. First, the current Rhine/Meuse/IJssel centre-distance screen assigns Cranendonck a persistent 1.197557 internal flood-depth-like value through T+72, even though the adopted Brabant-Zuidoost profile places the high-lying region outside direct sea/large-river flooding influence and identifies local brooks, extreme rain and wastewater overload as the relevant water pathways. Second, the neighbourhood allocator gives river, pluvial and heat exactly the same twenty-neighbourhood rank order and ranks an explicit ignition neighbourhood nineteenth despite the point lying inside a current TOP10NL forest object and multiple official combustible-nature areas. Cranendonck has genuine pluvial, brook, drought, heat, nature-fire, cross-border water, A2/rail, airport and industrial risk; suppressing an unsupported major-river scalar must therefore mean Unknown for unselected hydraulic events, not safe. Public provider areas, 69 water objects, 49 antenna registrations, ten schools and five government/service locations remain context only. Complete physical utility topology, live state, backup, stocks, crews and restoration commitments are unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented; all road-derived utility transfers remain correctly labeled logical proxies.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028
supports: The adopted profile includes Cranendonck among the 21 municipalities, identifies Kempen Airport at Budel near the Belgian border, and covers all-hazard and vital-service dependencies relevant to the first 72 hours.

The profile describes the region's relatively high position as outside direct influence from sea and large-river flooding while retaining extreme rainfall and smaller rivers/brooks, low areas, routes, wastewater and utility cascades as relevant pathways. That supports a direct contradiction check against a generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity field, not a claim that Cranendonck is water-safe.

Forest/heath, nature fire, storm, heat/drought, winter weather, hazardous transport, aviation, industrial incidents, cyber, electricity, water, telecom, mobility, wastewater, care and supply continuity are strategic scenario context. The PDF has a four-year planning edition, no live event API and no blanket machine-data licence or operational update cadence established here.

The profile records that an unknown substance completely disrupted the biological process at RWZI Soerendonk in 2018 and that restart took about two weeks; this is historical mechanism evidence, not present operating state or a generic restoration commitment.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatvisie Klimaatbestendig Cranendonck and official 2019 stress-test map package
supports: The official vision distinguishes heat, drought, extreme rainfall, overland flow and water-safety maps. It reports local heat amplification in the cores and industrial areas, with parts of Maarheeze, Budel and Budel-Schoot materially warmer, and identifies older residents as more vulnerable.

It identifies drought-sensitive sandy soils and ecologically sensitive Buulder Aa/Strijper Aa valleys, records nature fires near Budel and Maarheeze in 2018/2019, and locates extreme-rain problems especially in Budel and Maarheeze rather than establishing one common neighbourhood order.

Its water-over-street/stress-test context indicates local depths from centimetres toward roughly 30 cm in every core, possible emergency-access pressure on Grootschoterweg between Budel and Budel-Schoot, brook overflow near Buulder Aa, Strijper Aa and Sterkselsche Aa, and route effects toward Someren.

The current landing page is https://www.cranendonck.nl/klimaatvisie and the official map attachments are indexed at https://cranendonck.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl/Agenda/Index/bcad4570-53fc-42b1-907f-74af38c1f75d. The public PDFs are dated planning/context evidence; no public native GIS API, explicit redistribution licence or fixed refresh cadence was established, so they should validate rather than silently drive parcel-level T+0–72 values.

evidenceSources.title: Verbreed gemeentelijk rioleringsplan Cranendonck 2021–2025
supports: The official HTML/XML/download publication inventories approximately 80.567 km combined sewer, 22.435 km stormwater sewer, 16.500 km foul-water sewer, 64.463 km pressure sewer, 323 pressure units, 20 main pumping stations, 21 combined overflows, 14 separated/IT overflows, about 200 km watercourses and about 14 km culverts.

Twenty-three pump-containing installations are connected to AquaView++ telemetry and municipal pumps/pressure units are represented in SAM; the plan also describes measurement collaboration with Waterschap De Dommel and Brabant Water. These operational systems are not presented as open licensed topology/state APIs.

Cross-border water matters locally: streams entering from Belgium feed the Strijper Aa/Buulder Aa system. Administrative GM1706, Dutch road links and centre-distance river screens therefore do not capture the hydrological or response catchment.

The publication is a dated 2021–2025 management plan rather than a current incident feed. GWSW is the preferred open standard route where a current municipality-authorized export is available, but missing public topology, telemetry, controls and state remain Unknown rather than zero.

evidenceSources.title: Rioolwaterzuivering Soerendonk and national IMWA/DAMO public water registers
evidenceSources.edition: Current public pages/register snapshots inspected 2 September 2026
supports: RWZI Soerendonk serves Budel, Budel-Schoot, Budel-Dorplein, Gastel, Maarheeze and Soerendonk; sewage is pumped to the plant except that Maarheeze is conveyed by gravity. The published design is 38,000 population equivalents and 1,830 cubic metres per hour, with treated effluent discharged to the Buulder Aa.

Machine access is available through HWH Kunstwerken IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and Waterketen DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 under CC BY-SA 4.0. Kunstwerken is published weekly; DAMO contributor completeness and cadence vary and must travel with each snapshot.

The deployed GM1706 boundary context contains 69 display-only objects: four sewer pumps, RWZI Soerendonk, one surface-water pump and 63 weirs. The six non-weir records are marked realised, but presence/status does not establish topology, capacity for every object, setpoint, operating condition, emergency power or first-72-hour restoration; the different-scope municipal inventory proves public-register absence cannot mean no asset.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, cumulative burden, route bounds, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1706 pnpm audit:model passed both focused coverage tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 30.64 seconds (30.43 seconds test execution).
Every preset at intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every required checkpoint.

Repeated frames are deterministic; outputs are finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity; all eight headline pressure weights participate and close to one.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciles population 21,665, affected population 14,520 and all eight demand/delivery balances, with maximum observed floating-point discrepancy 3.55e-15.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The unselected major-river field, common neighbourhood allocator and source-insensitive wildfire map contradict Cranendonck's official regional and local evidence.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-472 derives named-major-river exposure from municipality-reference-point distance to three approximate national line segments. GM1706 is absent from the audited exclusion list even though E03 identifies no direct sea/large-river influence for this high-lying region.

At T+24 and T+72 the canonical river preset therefore retains internal flood-depth-like proxy 1.197557, severity 0.372084 and zero recovery for every service, without a selected connected Buulder Aa/Strijper Aa/Sterkselsche Aa/Meuse event, controls, arrival, depth, duration or recession surface.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3651-3664 derives one hazardSeed from city seed, scenario seed and region id; hazard type and source geometry do not enter the local multiplier. River, pluvial and heat therefore rank all twenty neighbourhoods identically: Budel first, then Klein-Schoot, Verspreide huizen Gastelse Hei, Soerendonk and Industrieterrein Den Engelsman Rondven, while Verspreide huizen in het Oosten is nineteenth and Verspreide huizen Hugten twentieth.

E04 instead locates different heat, drought, extreme-rain, access and brook-overflow patterns. Its old point/context maps are not current zonal truth, but they falsify any claim that the common order was evidence-derived.

A focused synthetic T+24 ignition [5.623618463418623, 51.26502712889067] lies inside TOP10NL naaldbos object 106330695 and BU17060009 Verspreide huizen in het Oosten. Direct fire is 0.563590 and city severity 0.555653, but the source neighbourhood ranks nineteenth at 0.457240 while Budel ranks first at 0.653369. E07 independently identifies multiple official combustible-nature areas in GM1706.
River emits derived-screening and pluvial/heat/wildfire synthetic evidence, so these unsupported neighbourhood ranks must not drive dispatch, evacuation or resource prioritization.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and preserve confidence, dependency order, operational assumptions and counterfactual scope.

notes: For river flooding, internal flood-depth-like stress 1.197557 and severity 0.372084 remain active through T+72 and recoveryProgress remains exactly zero for all eight services; this avoids instantaneous rebuilding while forcing persists but the forcing itself is unsupported.

River power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/supply availability stays 0.638610/0.579325/0.406161/0.758368/0.541416/0.516819/0.507188 from T+24 to T+72, while facilities falls from 0.651102 to 0.490250 through dependency dynamics. Affected population increases from 8,498 to 9,185 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours from 176,573 to 715,369.
Compound T+72 also retains active flood/cyber forcing, zero recovery progress for all services, pressure 0.632594 and 904,953 cumulative event-attributable person-hours.

The historical roughly two-week RWZI Soerendonk restart demonstrates that prolonged subsystem recovery is plausible under a specific biological disruption; it does not validate generic service curves, the river amplitude or present plant state.
Other preset recovery curves are bounded scenario assumptions. They must not be shown as Enexis, Brabant Water, Ziggo, De Dommel, municipality, rail or emergency-service restoration forecasts.

findings.summary: A coarse Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity field creates persistent direct river-flood impact in Cranendonck despite the adopted regional profile excluding direct large-river influence.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-472 derives exposure from the municipality reference point and three approximate national line segments; the municipality-specific safety exclusions at lines 439-460 omit GM1706. The canonical river run therefore reports internal flood-depth-like proxy 1.197557, severity 0.372084, T+24/T+72 pressure 0.418401/0.440920, affected population 8,498/9,185 and cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours 176,573/715,369, with every service recoveryProgress zero. E03 says Brabant-Zuidoost's high position lies outside direct sea and large-river influence; E04-E06 instead establish local extreme rain, Buulder Aa/Strijper Aa/Sterkselsche Aa, Belgian-fed brooks, sewer/RWZI and access pathways. No named connected hydraulic event, defence/control state, depth, arrival, duration or recession surface supports the displayed value. This is a municipality-specific false-positive manifestation of a shared screening rule, not evidence that Cranendonck is flood-safe.
findings.action: Before release, add GM1706 to the independently audited direct-major-river suppression until the proximity rule is replaced. Render unavailable local hydraulic-event coverage as Unknown/numerically neutral and keep pluvial, brook, drainage, access and indirect supply pathways visibly unresolved. Durable integration must require a named, connected, versioned LIWO/De Dommel/authorized event with units, resolution, NoData, controls, arrival and recession; run focused GM1706 and national regressions.

findings.summary: One hazard-independent neighbourhood hash makes Cranendonck river, pluvial and heat maps exactly rank-identical despite distinct official local hazard patterns.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3651-3664 uses one hazardSeed based on city seed, scenario seed and region id; hazard type/source geometry is absent. River, pluvial and heat all rank the same twenty neighbourhoods, led by Budel, Klein-Schoot, Verspreide huizen Gastelse Hei, Soerendonk and Industrieterrein Den Engelsman Rondven, with Verspreide huizen in het Oosten nineteenth and Verspreide huizen Hugten twentieth. E04 separately maps/reports core and industrial heat, sandy-soil/ecological drought, extreme-rain hotspots particularly in Budel/Maarheeze, Grootschoterweg access and brook overflow. The dated maps are validation context, not current zonal truth, but show the common ordering is synthetic rather than evidence-derived.
findings.action: Until hazard-specific geometry is integrated, grey or label neighbourhood ranks unsupported and prohibit operational prioritization. Prefer versioned RWS 70 mm/2 h WMS/GeoTIFF plus AHN and an authorized current local/De Dommel layer for pluvial/flow, separately sourced heat/drought surfaces, and selected water events. Pin event/version/reference date/units/resolution/licence, compute polygon-aware zonal values and preserve every NoData pixel as Unknown.

findings.summary: An explicit ignition inside official forest in Verspreide huizen in het Oosten does not control the displayed local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies TOP10NL naaldbos object d4fa0abb-7833-55f4-9bf3-fc5b6af9786f and focused source [5.623618463418623, 51.26502712889067] inside BU17060009 Verspreide huizen in het Oosten; E07 identifies multiple Cranendonck combustible-nature polygons. findings.summary: Public water objects and the named RWZI catchment improve context but do not establish Cranendonck drainage/wastewater topology, control state or restoration.
findings.evidence: E05 inventories a substantially larger and differently scoped municipal sewer/water system; E06 contributes four sewer pumps, RWZI Soerendonk, one surface-water pump and 63 weirs as deployed display-only context. Public-register absence is not no asset.
findings.action: Keep HWH IMWA/DAMO objects non-causal. Prefer a current municipality-authorized GWSW export and security-reviewed De Dommel connectivity/state input, with units, controls, topology, cadence and licence. findings.summary: Cranendonck's two A2 logical links pass section-level NWB identity checks but omit local, cross-border, rail and airport dependencies and cannot serve as utility topology.
findings.evidence: E02's live official NWB OGC records confirm all eight cited source wvk IDs use wegnummer 002/routeltr A/routenr 2. The generated Heeze-Leende and Weert links total 3.306 km and nominal capacity 520. All eight services share these road records and correctly emit transferSemantics logical-proxy; the values are neither vehicle throughput nor physical power/water/gas/telecom flow.

Restrict the road graph to mobility/access semantics and keep every non-road service connection as a labeled logical transfer proxy until authorized topology exists.

findings.summary: Provider polygons, antennas, schools and public-service records do not resolve Cranendonck utility, care, communications or household continuity.

Compound T+24 power 0.421364, water 0.388296, gas 0.542833, telecom 0.184832, facilities 0.395533 and supply 0.350118 are synthetic balances, not provider/facility observations.
findings.action: Keep provider and public registries display-only with publisher, edition, retrieval time, coverage and licence. Use capacity, state, backup, stock and restoration only from authorized operator/GHOR/municipal exercise inputs; otherwise retain the smallest service-specific synthetic prior and explicit Unknown.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and remote coastal/wildfire effects are bounded exercises but not calibrated Cranendonck forecasts or probabilities.
findings.evidence: E03-E04 establish these hazard families and local/regional cascade relevance. Canonical peaks are storm 0.655012, heat 0.696439, winter 0.717805, cyber 0.434042, remote Groningen-centred earthquake 0.004294, wildfire 0.116821 and coastal 0.021316. Coastal direct water is zero and its T+24 effect is a wind tail; canonical wildfire has zero direct flame and remote smoke/drought. Untargeted cyber assigns generic exposure, and meteorological values are deterministic equations rather than valid-time KNMI observations. These are conditional exercise consequences, not annual likelihood, live weather, attack intelligence or outage forecasts.
findings.action: Keep scenario, observation and probability labels distinct. Allow source/target selection; integrate versioned KNMI observed/forecast inputs only with valid time, licence and coverage, and use aviation, industrial, underground/cyber effects only through selected expert scenarios or authorized aggregate fragility envelopes.

findings.summary: The current adapter and audit preserve null, empty-coverage, NoData and display-only semantics instead of silently turning missing evidence into zero or truth.
findings.evidence: District-heating share and public-charging count remain null in all twenty neighbourhoods; cars per household remains null in nine; other incomplete CBS attributes remain null. findings.summary: The deterministic ten-scenario contract, zero-intensity baseline, causal ledgers, reconciliation and sustained-water recovery guard pass for GM1706.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passes 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services. All zero-intensity runs are exactly zero for severity, peak, affected population and cumulative event-attributable person-hours; repeated frames, finite bounds, monotonic accumulation and route bounds pass. Compound T+24 reconciles 21,665 people, 14,520 affected and every demand/delivery ledger within 3.55e-15; all eleven map layers are invariant. Active river/compound water holds every service recoveryProgress at zero through T+72. Explanations label person-hours, operational multipliers, delayed interventions and road-derived transfers as scenario/proxy semantics.
findings.action: Preserve these regressions while correcting unsupported major-river forcing, common hazard allocation and source-insensitive wildfire mapping; a passing arithmetic contract must remain separate from physical validation.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Cranendonck disaster, outage, casualty, evacuation, welfare or restoration dataset.
The 2025 generalized CBS boundary is suitable for municipal aggregation but not parcel hydraulics, cross-border catchments, asset ownership, response jurisdiction or exact incident geometry.
The municipality's 2019 climate/stress-test maps and 2021–2025 sewer plan are dated planning context, not current observations, native licensed zonal GIS or live operational state.
RWS 70 mm/2 h and AHN are national scenario/terrain layers; they do not independently provide a local event, sewer controls, brook levels, arrival or recession, and NoData remains Unknown.
TOP10NL forest and IPO combustible-nature polygons are static eligibility context rather than live fuel, moisture, spread, suppression or access state; the focused eastern ignition is synthetic.
HWH/provider/antenna/facility/station/GTFS records are partial dated context, not complete topology, capacity, operating state, backup, stock or restoration commitments.
No reviewed public safe source supplies complete Enexis, Brabant Water, municipal sewer, gas, telecom, care, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behavior, medically dependent people, responders, mutual aid, shelters, airport/rail operations, Belgian dependencies, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, crew travel, repair priorities and visitor/daytime demand remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
